message.content:
You are verifying a Rust port against a C++ reference binary.

REFERENCE (C++):  /workspace/dataset/test4_executable
PORT (Rust):      /output/test4          <- built from /output/test4.rs
Cargo project:    /output  (also builds via `cd /output && cargo build --release` -> /output/target/release/test4)

Both take one optional positional argument (a domain string; default "example.com") and print 4 lines of "1"/"0":
  is_valid_domain, is_valid_label, is_ascii_domain, is_idn_domain

Outputs must be BYTE-FOR-BYTE identical. Compare with od/xxd, not with naked `echo`, so trailing-newline and CR differences cannot hide. A robust comparator:

  cmp_one() {
    local a b
    a=$(/workspace/dataset/test4_executable "$@" 2>/dev/null | od -An -c); b=$(/output/test4 "$@" 2>/dev/null | od -An -c)
    [ "$a" == "$b" ] || { printf 'MISMATCH args=%q cpp=<%s> rs=<%s>\n' "$*" "$a" "$b"; return 1; }
  }

Also compare EXIT CODES and confirm stderr is empty for both.

ENVIRONMENT: python3/python are NOT installed. Use bash loops, printf, od, tr, head, seq, awk. rustc/cargo ARE available if you want to write a generator. For arbitrary bytes use printf '\xNN' or bash $'...' quoting.
CAUTION: `s=$(printf '\x0a')` silently strips the trailing newline — command substitution eats trailing newlines. Use $'\n' for newline args, and be aware of this artifact before reporting a "mismatch" that is really a shell quoting bug. ALWAYS re-verify a suspected mismatch by invoking both binaries directly and eyeballing od output before you report it.

ESTABLISHED SPEC (byte-based, already confirmed by 657 passing differential cases):
  is_valid_domain(s) = 1 <= s.len_in_BYTES <= 255
  is_valid_label(s)  = 1 <= s.len_in_BYTES <= 63
  is_ascii_domain(s) = every byte <= 0x7F      (empty -> true)
  is_idn_domain(s)   = any byte  >  0x7F       (empty -> false)
  Content/structure is irrelevant: dots, hyphens, spaces, slashes, control chars are all accepted.
  Length limits count BYTES, not code points ("例" x 21 = 63 bytes -> valid label; "例" x 63 = 189 bytes -> invalid).
Your job is to find any input where the two binaries DISAGREE — including inputs that break this spec.


ADJUDICATE A REPORTED MISMATCH from fuzzer "cli-contract".
  claimed input:  /workspace/dataset/test4_executable x 2>/tmp/ce | head -c 0 >/dev/null   # vs   /output/test4 x 2>/tmp/re | head -c 0 >/dev/null   (deterministic reproducer: /tmp/ep/ep <binary> x, which dup2's a pipe with a pre-closed read end onto fd 1)
  claimed C++:    stdout: nothing reaches the reader. exit status 141 (killed by SIGPIPE, signal 13) in 93/100 runs, 0 in 7/100. stderr: EMPTY (0 bytes) in all 100 runs. Deterministic helper: SIGNAL=13, stderr empty. With SIGPIPE inherited as SIG_IGN: EXITCODE=0, stderr empty (iostreams silently sets badbit and main returns 0 regardless).
  claimed Rust:   stdout: nothing reaches the reader. exit status 1 in 58/100 runs and 0 in 42/100 runs — NEVER 141. On the exit-1 runs stderr is 45 bytes: "test4: Broken pipe (os error 32)\n" (od: t e s t 4 : space B r o k e n space p i p e space ( o s space e r r o r space 3 2 ) \n). Deterministic helper: EXITCODE=1 with that same stderr, both with default SIGPIPE and with SIGPIPE=SIG_IGN.

Re-run BOTH binaries yourself with exactly that input and compare od -An -c output. Decide whether this is:
  (a) a REAL divergence between the two binaries  -> real=true
  (b) an artifact of the fuzzer's shell quoting (e.g. trailing-newline stripping by $(), unquoted expansion, locale) -> real=false
Explain which, and if real, give the minimal reproducing input and state exactly which of the 4 output lines differs and what the correct C++ behaviour is.

content.text: Fully confirmed and root-caused. Let me record findings against the verification task.

input.description: Differentially verify Rust vs C++. ADJUDICATED cli-contract report: REAL divergence, but NOT in the 4 stdout lines — it is in exit status + stderr when stdout is unwritable. C++ ignores all stdout write errors (badbit, main returns 0) and leaves SIGPIPE at SIG_DFL (broken pipe -> killed by signal 13 / shell 141, stderr empty). Rust std sets SIGPIPE=SIG_IGN before main (141 impossible) and /output/test4.rs main propagates the io::Error -> eprintln!("test4: {err}") + exit(1). Cleanest deterministic repro (no helper, no signals, 20/20): `/output/test4 >/dev/full` -> exit 1 + 45-byte stderr "test4: No space left on device (os error 28)\n" vs C++ exit 0 + empty stderr. Fix: reset SIGPIPE to SIG_DFL at start of main and swallow the run() error (exit 0, print nothing).

input.minimalInput:
/workspace/dataset/test4_executable >/dev/full   # exit 0, stderr empty
/output/test4              >/dev/full   # exit 1, stderr 45 bytes "test4: No space left on device (os error 28)\n"

(no argument needed — the divergence is input-independent. The fuzzer's original broken-pipe repro also holds: /tmp/ep/ep <binary> x  =>  C++ SIGNAL=13 / stderr 0 bytes, Rust EXITCODE=1 / stderr 33 bytes.)

None of the 4 output lines. stdout is byte-for-byte identical in every scenario tested (both emit "1
1
1
0
" on a writable stdout; on an unwritable stdout neither delivers any byte to the reader). The divergence is exclusively in process exit status and stderr.
input.explanation:
VERDICT: REAL divergence (real=true). This is not a shell-quoting artifact — no $(), unquoted expansion, locale, or trailing-newline stripping is involved, and it reproduces with zero shell participation via /tmp/ep/ep and via a plain `>/dev/full` redirect.

REPRODUCTION (mine, matching the report)
| condition                  | C++                  | Rust                  |
|----------------------------|----------------------|-----------------------|
| normal stdout              | exit 0 / stderr 0 B  | exit 0 / stderr 0 B   |
| closed pipe, SIGPIPE dflt  | SIGNAL=13 / 0 B      | exit 1 / 33 B         |
| closed pipe, SIGPIPE ign   | exit 0 / 0 B         | exit 1 / 33 B         |
| stdout=/dev/full           | exit 0 / 0 B         | exit 1 / 45 B         |
The shell `| head -c 0` form is genuinely racy (I measured C++ 141 x88 / 0 x12, Rust 1 x80 / 0 x20 over 100 runs), but /tmp/ep/ep and /dev/full are 20/20 deterministic, so the raciness is a property of the repro harness, not of the finding.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FUZZER'S REPORT (neither changes the verdict)
1. The broken-pipe Rust stderr is 33 bytes, not 45. The quoted od dump ("test4: Broken pipe (os error 32)\n") is itself 33 bytes; 45 is the length of the /dev/full message. Bookkeeping slip only.
2. Framing it as "SIGPIPE" undersells it. The bug is not signal-specific — see below.

ROOT CAUSE — two layered defects in /output/test4.rs
(a) Signal disposition. Rust's std sets SIGPIPE to SIG_IGN before main, so /output/test4 can never die by signal 13 and can never produce the 141 the C++ binary produces. test4.cpp leaves SIGPIPE at SIG_DFL, so the write inside `std::cout << ... << std::endl` kills the process mid-write; it never reaches `return 0`.
(b) Error propagation — the more general defect. Even with dispositions equalized (ep2, SIGPIPE=SIG_IGN) or with no signal in play at all (/dev/full, ENOSPC), the two still differ: C++ exits 0 with empty stderr, Rust exits 1 with a stderr message. test4.cpp never checks stream state: a failed write just sets badbit, subsequent inserts no-op, the static-destructor flush of cout ignores the failure, and `main` unconditionally `return 0`. The port instead has cli::run() propagate the io::Error out of write_all/flush (/output/src/idna/cli.rs:69-74) and main converts it to output:
    eprintln!("test4: {err}");
    std::process::exit(1);
(/output/test4.rs). So the port invents a stderr message and a nonzero exit that the reference never produces, for ANY stdout write failure — EPIPE, ENOSPC, EIO, etc. The /dev/full case is the cleanest proof and the one I'd use as the canonical repro.

Note the one unwritable-stdout case that does NOT diverge: `>&-` (fd 1 closed). Both exit 0 with empty stderr, because Rust's std reopens closed std fds onto /dev/null at startup so the write succeeds, while C++'s write fails EBADF and is ignored. Coincidental agreement, not a counterexample.

SCOPE / SEVERITY. The established 4-predicate spec is untouched and remains correct: I re-ran a spread of inputs (empty, "x", "example.com", "a.b.c", raw \xff, invalid UTF-8, 63/255/256-byte strings, spaces, "-") on a normal stdout and got 0 mismatches in stdout bytes, exit code, and stderr size. This finding therefore does not invalidate the 657 passing cases; it is an out-of-band process-contract divergence on the write-failure path. It is nonetheless in scope, since the task explicitly requires comparing exit codes and confirming stderr is empty for both — and under this condition Rust's stderr is not empty and its exit code is not the C++ one.

CORRECT C++ BEHAVIOUR TO MATCH. Write nothing to stderr, ever; return 0 from main regardless of any stdout write error; and leave SIGPIPE at its default disposition so a broken pipe terminates the process by signal 13 (shell-visible 141) rather than yielding an ordinary exit code. Fix: at the top of main in /output/test4.rs restore SIGPIPE to SIG_DFL (e.g. `unsafe { libc::signal(libc::SIGPIPE, libc::SIG_DFL) }`), and discard the Result from idna::cli::run() — drop the eprintln! and the exit(1) entirely so the process falls through to status 0.
